Resume

Summary

Enterprise Web Architect, TDD Advocate, and Community Contributor with 30+ years of experience building, securing, and scaling high-availability digital platforms. Prominent Drupal open-source steward (16+ years), maintaining critical ecosystem projects including Easy Breadcrumb, a module natively shipping with the new Drupal CMS initiative. Expert across all generations of Drupal (including modern Drupal 10/11 architectures, TDD integration frameworks, and forward-looking Drupal 12 development). Pioneer in frontier AI implementations within the Drupal ecosystem, decoupled React frameworks, enterprise cloud management (Acquia, AWS, Pantheon), and large-scale legacy data migrations.

Technical Skills

  • Modern Drupal Architecture: Drupal 10, 11, & 12 Readiness, Symfony Components, Plugin API, Hook System Deprecations, Configuration Management, Composer Workflows, Twig 3
  • Automated Testing & TDD: PHPUnit, Static Analysis (PHPStan), Drupal Kernel & Functional Integration Tests, FunctionalJavascript Tests, Nightwatch.js, Cypress, Selenium, Behat, Sonar
  • AI & Frontier Technologies: Drupal AI Core and Contrib Ecosystem, Large Language Model (LLM) Integrations, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Workflows, Vector Embeddings
  • Front-End & Decoupled: React.js, ES6+ JavaScript, Node.js, Component-Driven Styling (KSS, Storybook, Canvas Workbench), HTML5, SASS/CSS3, Figma, Photoshop, Illustrator
  • Data & Infrastructure: Apache Solr Indexing, MySQL/MariaDB/PostGres, MS SQL Migration, Apache, Nginx, Docker, DDEV/Lando, SSH, Bash Scripting, Acquia Cloud, AWS, Pantheon, CI/CD Pipelines
  • Specializations: Core/Contrib Module Maintenance, Web Accessibility (WCAG/Section 508), Enterprise Security Hardening, REST/GraphQL APIs

Open Source Stewardship & Community Impact

Project Maintainer, Easy Breadcrumb (Core Ecosystem Module) | 2017 – Present

  • Actively maintain and architect Easy Breadcrumb, a foundational navigation module officially integrated into the core-curated Drupal CMS distribution.
  • Shipped dozens of performance, schema, testing, and architectural optimization improvements over recent months to improve seamless out-of-the-box compatibility for 100,000+ global installs.
  • Audit codebase continually for upcoming deprecations to guarantee a zero-friction upgrade path to the upcoming Drupal 12 lifecycle.

Frontier AI Innovation & Community Collaboration

  • Active Member, Drupal AI Learners Club: Collaborate directly with global ecosystem innovators within official Drupal Slack channels to discuss, test, and implement bleeding-edge AI initiatives and agentic workflows.
  • Versed in leveraging Drupal AI modules to integrate frontier models, automate content generation matrices, build conversational search interfaces, and architect RAG solutions inside enterprise web applications.

Additional Project Maintenance & Contributions

  • Maintainer: Config Suite, Drupal 8 Contrib Porting Tracker.
  • Core Readiness: Made major contributions to the Drupal 8 Multilingual Demo project, preparing Drupal 8 for multilingual deployment during alpha and beta core cycles.
  • Security & Docs: Contributed to security advisories and numerous technical documentation edits on Drupal.org. Credited in resolving over 200 public issues.

Professional Experience

Redaptive.com | Staff Software Engineer | Nov 2018 – Jun 2023

  • Served firstly as the solo Front-end and Drupal Architect, scaling the platform and engineering operations from a single-developer model to a high-performing global team of 10+ engineers.
  • Engineered decoupled React.js interfaces backed by enterprise Drupal installations on Acquia Cloud, integrating real-time AWS data streams and collaborating cross-functionally with an internal Java engineering team.
  • Designed, documented, and maintained the foundational core codebases, establishing the architectural standards, code style guides, and Git workflows for the entire growing department.
  • Spearheaded engineering knowledge management and project governance across the Atlassian suite, creating comprehensive technical documentation in Confluence and structuring agile workflows in Jira.

Zicasso.com | Senior Drupal Developer | 2016 – Aug 2018

  • Maintained a high-traffic, highly complex transactional e-commerce platform connecting global travelers with agencies.
  • Built custom architectural components including automated invoicing mechanisms and secure internal messaging systems.
  • Developed a component-driven front-end ecosystem via a living style guide and design pattern library using KSS.
  • Implemented and executed a custom multi-variate (A/B) testing engine to continuously optimize user conversion funnels utilizing Pantheon Multisite and Google Analytics.

SunPower.com | Senior Drupal Developer | 2015 – 2016

  • Led development for the SunPower "Savings Calculator," which won the 2016 Oracle Markie Award for Best Web or Commerce Experience.
  • Engineered an internationalized multi-site architecture, developing streamlined multilingual translation workflows on Acquia.

Alzforum.org | Senior Drupal Developer | 2013 – 2014

  • Served as lead developer rebuilding a 15-year-old scientific networking platform into an enterprise Drupal architecture hosted on Acquia.
  • Migrated over 150,000 legacy content items from an aging MSSQL database; leveraged Apache Solr to perform complex scientific database searches.
  • Integrated a 3rd-party vendor's responsive template into a custom theme, and built a custom publishing/review system that integrated with PubMed APIs to pull in nightly scientific updates.

Early Career & Enterprise Contract Experience | Senior Drupal Developer | 2012 – 2013

  • University of Phoenix (Research Portal): Collaborated directly with Acquia teams to develop and launch an agile, responsive portal for research fellows under highly aggressive timelines.
  • General Electric (Inside GE Software): Built an internal, responsive corporate platform using custom installation profiles, heavily leveraging panels/ctools for a highly flexible content editing experience.
  • Johnson & Johnson: Engineered mobile-responsive Drupal sites for One Touch diabetes testers and for Children With Diabetes, crafting multi-step AJAX-driven forms with custom Google Analytics tracking funnels.

Additional Information

  • Languages: Native English; conversational proficiency in basic Spanish (read, write, speak).
  • Interests: Science, health and safety, communication, music, and open-source mentoring.

item.title: Testing with DDev, Gitlab, and serving Drupal from a subfolder instead of a subdomain
item.description:
Testing with DDev, Gitlab, and serving Drupal from a subfolder instead of a subdomain

While working on the Easy Breadcrumb module for Drupal, I came across a situation where a test was failling on Gitlab but was passing with DDev: https://www.drupal.org/project/easy_breadcrumb/issues/3615550

The difference that mattered was that Gitlab serves the site from http://localhost/web for testing and locally it gets served from a fully qualified domain name, ie. http://ddev.site.example.com.

Getting the test to fail locally

Using firecow/gitlab-ci-local

To get the test to fail locally, I used the suggestions at https://project.pages.drupalcode.org/gitlab_templates/info/test-locally/ , which suggested firecow/gitlab-ci-local . I did get that working but I ran into a hitch. My work computer is a Mac with an ARM64 chip and gitlab-ci-local tries to install selenium/standalone-chrome:127.0, which doesn't support ARM64. I dug around and figured out that I could use selenium/standalone-chromium:latest instead by adding a few lines in .gitlab-ci.yml:

phpunit:
  services:
    - !reference [.with-database]
    - name: selenium/standalone-chromium:latest
      alias: selenium
      
# The lines below are to filter which tests run. In this case, only tests in the
# "redirect" group.
variables:
  _PHPUNIT_TESTGROUPS: "redirect"

Then, on the command line, to just run PHPUnit and not most of the other steps, I used the --stage flag to just run jobs in the test stage, which by default is just PHPUnit:

$ drupal-ci-local --stage=test

That worked and I was able to reproduce locally. But, it took about a minute to run the test instead of 2 or 3 seconds with DDev.

Using DDEV to serve a Drupal site from a subdirectory instead of a subdomain

This way is not perfect, but it worked well enough for me to use Xdebug when running tests and when browing the site in a browser.

The code below results in the site being served from a subdirectory named easy, ie. http://example.com/easy.

First, cd to root of project, then:

mkdir router
ls -s ./web ./router/easy

Then, in .ddev/config.yaml

docroot: router

Next, in settings.php

if (isset($GLOBALS['request'])) {
 $request = $GLOBALS['request'];
 $script_name = $request->server->get('SCRIPT_NAME');
 if ($script_name === '/easy/index.php' || $script_name === '/index.php') {
   $request->server->set('SCRIPT_NAME', '/easy/index.php');
 }
}

Then, in .ddev/nginx_full/nginx-site.conf, replace the section that starts with 'location /' to be like this instead:

   # 1. CSS/JS caches
   location ~* ^/easy/sites/.*/files/(css|js)/ {
       try_files $uri @rewrite;
       expires max;
       log_not_found off;
   }
   # 2. Image styles
   location ~* ^/easy/sites/.*/files/styles/ {
       try_files $uri @rewrite;
   }
   # 3. Clean URLs
   location /easy {
       try_files $uri $uri/ /easy/index.php?$query_string;
   }
   # 4. Fallback
   location @rewrite {
       rewrite ^/easy/(.*)$ /easy/index.php?$query_string;
   }

To run phpunit tests, pass in SIMPLETEST_BASE_URL.
Example which just runs ones test:

ddev exec SIMPLETEST_BASE_URL=http://localhost/easy vendor/bin/phpunit --bootstrap web/core/tests/bootstrap.php --filter testEasyBreadcrumbFollowRedirects web/modules/custom/easy_breadcrumb

item.title: Bash scripts for Drupal, DDEV, and Tome
item.description:
Bash scripts for Drupal, DDEV, and Tome

This website is made with Drupal. Local development is done with DDEV configured to use Orbstack for container management. The Tome Drupal module exports the dynamic site to a static site. Python is used to preview the site locally. Public hosting is provided free by Github.

Here are some custom bash aliases and functions I use to make common local tasks easy. Concurrently is used to run two processes in one terminal session.

alias brookemahoneycomCd='cd ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom'
brookemahoneycomLaunch () {
  # Starts Orbstack if it isn't running.
  orb
  brookemahoneycomCd
  cd drupal
  ddev launch
}

brookemahoneycomPreview () {
  brookemahoneycomCd
  cd docs
  concurrently 'python -m http.server' 'open "http://localhost:8000"'
}

brookemahoneycomBuild() {
  # Starts Orbstack if it isn't running.
  orb
  # Changes to the drupal directory.
  cd ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/drupal
  # Clears caches.
  ddev drush cr
  # Exports the site with Tome.
  ddev drush tome:static --uri=https://brookemahoney.com
  # Removes old docs directory.
  rm -rf ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/docs
  # Copies the Tome build directory to docs for Github hosting.
  cp -R ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/drupal/html ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/docs
  # Copies over static files, such as CNAME for Github hosting.
  cp -R ~/projects/brookemahoneycom/sync/ ~/Sites/brookemahoneycom/docs
}

All the code for the Drupal install is in this site's Github repo.
